'''Victor Wembanyama''' ({{IPAc-en|ˌ|w|ɛ|m|b|ə|n|ˈ|j|ɑː|m|ə}} {{respelling|WEM|bən|YAH|mə}};<ref>{{cite press release |author=<!--Not stated--> |title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide |publisher=National Basketball Association |date=24 October 2023 |access-date=17 May 2024}}</ref> {{IPA|fr|viktɔʁ wɛmbanjama|lang}}; born 4 January 2004), nicknamed "'''Wemby'''"<ref>{{cite web |last1=Williams |first1=Randall |title=Victor Wembanyama Sets Course to Become a Basketball Billionaire Unlike Any Other |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2024-01-05/how-wemby-can-make-1-billion-in-basketball-earnings-in-nba-career |website=[[Bloomberg News]] |access-date=5 January 2024 |date=5 January 2024 |archive-date=5 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240105000546/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2024-01-05/how-wemby-can-make-1-billion-in-basketball-earnings-in-nba-career |url-status=live }}</ref> and "'''the Alien'''",<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dodson |first=Aaron |date=26 July 2024 |title=How Victor Wembanyama's unearthly size and still-growing feet made him Nike's 'Alien' |url=https://andscape.com/features/victor-wembanyama-nike-alien-logo/ |access-date=2 February 2025 |website=Andscape |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Walsh |first=Erin |title=Spurs' Victor Wembanyama 'Not Really a Big Fan' of Unicorn Nickname; Prefers 'Alien' |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10096656-spurs-victor-wembanyama-not-really-a-big-fan-of-unicorn-nickname-prefers-alien |access-date=2 February 2025 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}}</ref> is a French professional [[basketball]] player for the [[San Antonio Spurs]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He was selected [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall]] by the Spurs in the [[2023 NBA draft]] and is considered one of the best basketball prospects ever due to his rare combination of height, agility, and skills.<ref>{{Cite news |date=16 June 2023 |last=Adi  |first=Joseph |title=Ranking the 20 best NBA Draft prospects since LeBron: Victor Wembanyama, AD, Zion at top with Scoot sliding in |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/ranking-the-20-best-nba-draft-prospects-since-lebron-victor-wembanyama-ad-zion-at-top-with-scoot-sliding-in/ |access-date=1 June 2026 |work=CBS Sports |language=en}}</ref> 

Wembanyama began his professional career at age 15 with [[Nanterre 92]] of the [[LNB Pro A]] in 2019. Two years later, he moved to [[ASVEL Basket|ASVEL]] and won the Pro A title in his only season with the team. In the [[2022–23 Pro A season|2022–23 season]], Wembanyama signed with [[Metropolitans 92]] and became the youngest player to win the [[LNB Pro A MVP|Pro A MVP]] award, while earning [[LNB Pro A Best Defender|Pro A Best Defender]] honours and leading the league in scoring, [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] and [[block (basketball)|blocks]]. He was unanimously named an [[LNB All-Star]] twice, winning the All-Star Game MVP once, and was a three-time [[LNB Pro A Best Young Player|Pro A Best Young Player]] from 2021 to 2023.

Following a historic rookie season in the NBA in which he led the league in [[Block (basketball)|blocks]] per game, Wembanyama was unanimously named the [[2023–24 NBA season|2024]] [[NBA Rookie of the Year]] and became the first rookie and youngest player ever to be named to the [[NBA All-Defensive Team|All-Defensive First Team]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lopez |first=Andrew |date=6 May 2024 |title=Spurs' Victor Wembanyama voted unanimous Rookie of Year |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/40096225/spurs-victor-wembanyama-named-unanimous-rookie-year |access-date=7 May 2024 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=7 May 2024 |title=Rudy Gobert wins record-tying 4th Defensive Player of the Year award. Victor Wembanyama finishes 2nd |url=https://apnews.com/article/nba-defensive-player-of-year-rudy-gobert-wembanyama-1d7846b4f8094579906c09619134bda1 |access-date=10 May 2024 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref> During the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], Wembanyama became the youngest and first unanimous winner of the [[NBA Defensive Player of the Year|Defensive Player of the Year]] award.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Spurs' Victor Wembanyama named 2025-26 Kia NBA Defensive Player of the Year {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/news/kia-nba-defensive-player-of-the-year-award-2025-26 |access-date=20 April 2026 |website=NBA |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Soto |first=Andrés |date=20 April 2026 |title=Victor Wembanyama makes history as NBA Defensive Player of the Year |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/spurs/2026/04/20/san-antonio-spurs-victor-wembanyama-defensive-player-year/89694655007/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260422024818/https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/spurs/2026/04/20/san-antonio-spurs-victor-wembanyama-defensive-player-year/89694655007/ |archive-date=22 April 2026 |access-date=30 April 2026 |work=USA TODAY |language=en-US}}</ref> That same year, he led the Spurs to the [[2026 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] in his first postseason appearance.

Wembanyama also plays for the [[France men's national basketball team|French national team]], with whom he won a silver medal at the [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2024 Olympics]]. At the youth level, he led his team to two silver medals, including at the [[2021 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2021 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]], where he set the [[FIBA]] record for blocks per game in a single tournament.

==Professional career==
===Nanterre 92 (2019–2021)===
In the 2019–20 season, Wembanyama gained his first professional experience with the [[Nanterre 92]] senior team under head coach [[Pascal Donnadieu]],<ref name=jaquin/> receiving limited playing time in two games.<ref name=realgm/> He primarily competed in LNB Espoirs, the French under-21 league, and also played for the under-18 team.<ref name=jaquin/><ref>{{cite web |title=Nanterre : Victor Wembanyama dans le groupe professionnel contre Orléans |url=https://www.bebasket.fr/nanterre-victor-wembanyama-dans-le-groupe-professionnel-contre-orleans/ |publisher=BeBasket |access-date=8 January 2023 |language=fr |date=26 October 2019 |archive-date=8 January 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230108174828/https://www.bebasket.fr/nanterre-victor-wembanyama-dans-le-groupe-professionnel-contre-orleans/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Wembanyama made his professional debut on 29 October 2019, playing 31 seconds against [[Pallacanestro Brescia|Brescia]] in the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]]. At 15 years, nine months and 25 days old, he was the second-youngest player after [[Stefan Petković]] to play in the EuroCup.<ref>{{cite news |last=Lupo |first=Nicola |title=Nanterre: il 15enne Victor Wembanyama fa il suo debutto in EuroCup contro Brescia |url=https://sportando.basketball/nanterre-il-15enne-victor-wembanyama-fa-il-suo-debutto-in-eurocup-contro-brescia/ |newspaper=Sportando |access-date=11 January 2023 |language=Italian |date=29 October 2019 |archive-date=11 January 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230111164120/https://sportando.basketball/nanterre-il-15enne-victor-wembanyama-fa-il-suo-debutto-in-eurocup-contro-brescia/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In February 2020, Wembanyama played for Nanterre's under-18 team at the [[2019–20 Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament#Kaunas, Lithuania|Kaunas qualifying tournament]] for the [[2019–20 Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament|Adidas Next Generation Tournament]] (ANGT). On 8 February, he posted 22 [[point (basketball)|points]], 15 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] and an ANGT-record nine blocks in a win over the under-18 team of [[Basket Zaragoza|Zaragoza]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Victor Wembanyama, 16, has historic ANGT performance |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1019678/victor-wembanyama-16-has-historic-angt-performance/ |publisher=Eurohoops |access-date=8 February 2020 |date=8 February 2020 |archive-date=22 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230622142358/https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1019678/victor-wembanyama-16-has-historic-angt-performance/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Wembanyama averaged 15.8 points, 12 rebounds, 2.8 [[steal (basketball)|steals]], and six blocks per game in Kaunas, leading the tournament in blocks and earning all-tournament team honours.<ref>{{cite web |last=Hein |first=David |title=Tubelis takes home MVP as Rytas takes first place |url=https://www.adidasngt.com/u18/news/latest/i/adpcfgrt5nl3cg8p/tubelis-takes-home-mvp-as-rytas-takes-first-place |publisher=[[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament]] |access-date=18 October 2020 |date=9 February 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201018232953/https://www.adidasngt.com/u18/news/latest/i/adpcfgrt5nl3cg8p/tubelis-takes-home-mvp-as-rytas-takes-first-place |archive-date= 18 October 2020}}</ref> He finished the Espoirs season averaging 10.2 points, 4.9 rebounds and 3.3 blocks per game, mostly coming off the bench.<ref name="lnb">{{cite web |title=Victor Wembanyama |url=https://www.lnb.fr/elite/joueur/?id=8052 |publisher=[[Ligue nationale de basket]] |access-date=4 January 2023 |language=fr |archive-date=6 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221206014625/https://www.lnb.fr/elite/joueur/?id=8052 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 6 May 2024, Wembanyama was named the [[2023–24 NBA season|2024]] [[NBA Rookie of the Year Award|NBA Rookie of the Year]], becoming the sixth rookie to ever win the award by a unanimous vote.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Spurs' Victor Wembanyama voted unanimous Rookie of Year|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/40096225/spurs-victor-wembanyama-named-unanimous-rookie-year|date=6 May 2024|access-date=7 May 2024|website=espn.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=7 May 2024 |title=Wembanyama named unanimous NBA rookie of the year after stunning debut season |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/article/2024/may/06/wembanyama-named-unanimous-nba-rookie-of-the-year-after-stunning-debut-season}}</ref> He also joined [[Manute Bol]] as the only rookies in NBA history to lead the league in blocks per game and total blocks in a season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/inside-victor-wembanyama-rookie-of-the-year-numbers-feats|title=Inside Victor Wembanyama's historic Rookie of the Year numbers, feats|website=ClutchPoints|last=Ledesma|first=Hector|date=7 May 2024|access-date=7 May 2024}}</ref> Wembanyama also finished second place in voting for the 2024 [[NBA Defensive Player of the Year Award]], behind [[Rudy Gobert]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=7 May 2024 |title=Gobert ties NBA record with fourth DPOY award |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/40102549/timberwolves-rudy-gobert-named-defensive-player-year |access-date=8 May 2024 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> Wembanyama was named to the NBA All-Defensive First Team, becoming the first rookie and youngest player in NBA history to achieve this feat.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/spurs-news-victor-wembanyama-extends-san-antonios-all-defensive-team-dominance-historic-honor|title=Victor Wembanyama extends Spurs' All-Defensive Team dominance with historic honor|website=ClutchPoints|last=Ledesma|first=Hector|date=21 May 2024|access-date=22 May 2024}}</ref>

====2024–25 season: First All-Star selection and season-ending illness====
On 31 October 2024, Wembanyama had his second career five-by-five, putting up 25 points, nine rebounds, seven assists, five steals, and five blocks. He became the third player in NBA history to record multiple five-by-five games, joining [[Hakeem Olajuwon]] and [[Andrei Kirilenko]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Victor Wembanyama has second 5x5 game in Spurs' win vs. Jazz|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/42122849/victor-wembanyama-second-5x5-game-spurs-win-vs-jazz|work=ESPN.com|date=31 October 2024|access-date=31 October 2024}}</ref> On 4 November, Wembanyama put up a statline of 24 points, 13 rebounds, three assists, three steals and nine blocks, in a 113–104 loss against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Powell scores 23, Clippers rally from 26-point deficit to beat Spurs 113-104|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401704734 |work=ESPN.com|date=5 November 2024|access-date=10 November 2024}}</ref> On 9 November, Wembanyama put up 24 points, 16 rebounds, seven blocks, and shot six-of-nine from three-point range in a 111–110 loss to the [[Utah Jazz]]. He also became the first player in NBA history to have multiple games with 20+ points, 15+ rebounds, 5+ three-pointers, and 5+ blocks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/spurs-news-victor-wembanyama-bonkers-nba-history-latest-feat|title=Spurs' Victor Wembanyama makes bonkers NBA history with latest feat|website=ClutchPoints|last=Brown|first=Malik|date=10 November 2024|access-date=11 November 2024}}</ref> On 13 November, Wembanyama scored a career-high 50 points, including a career-high eight three-pointers in a 139–130 win over the [[Washington Wizards]]. Aged 20 years and 314 days, he also became the fourth-youngest player to score 50 points in an NBA game, as well as the first player in league history with 20 three-pointers and 13 blocks in a three-game span.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Wright|first=Michael|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/42378575/spurs-victor-wembanyama-scores-career-high-50-points-win-vs-wizards|title=Victor Wembanyama scores career-high 50 points in Spurs' win|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=13 November 2024|access-date=14 November 2024}}</ref>

On 21 December, Wembanyama posted 30 points and tied his career-high 10 blocks in a 114–94 win over the Portland Trail Blazers. He became just the sixth player in league history to record 30-plus points and 10-plus blocks in a game, joining Hakeem Olajuwon (5x), David Robinson (3x), [[Artis Gilmore]], Dwight Howard and [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar]]. At 20 years and 352 days old, Wembanyama is the youngest player to ever hit the mark, breaking Dwight Howard’s previous record by nearly two years. He became the first player with four 3-pointers and 10 blocks in a game in NBA history. Wembanyama also had a block in 62 straight games, surpassing the franchise record of 61 set by David Robinson.<ref>{{Cite web |date=22 December 2024 |title=Victor Wembanyama becomes the 6th NBA player with 30-point, 10-block game |url=https://www.nba.com/news/victor-wembanyama-30-point-10-block |access-date=22 December 2024 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On 25 December, he made his [[NBA Christmas games|Christmas Day]] debut, registering 42 points, 18 rebounds, 4 assists, and 4 blocks in a 117–114 loss to the [[New York Knicks]]. He became the third player in NBA history to score 40+ points and 15+ rebounds in a Christmas game, after [[Wilt Chamberlain]] (1959 and 1961) and [[Nikola Jokić]] (2022). He also scored the third-most points for a player in his Christmas Day debut, behind Chamberlain (45) and [[Tracy McGrady]] (43).<ref>{{Cite web|last=Wright|first=Michael C.|url=https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/victor-wembanyama-puts-42-points-christmas-day-debut/story?id=117108813|title=Victor Wembanyama puts up 42 points in Christmas Day debut|publisher=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]]|date=25 December 2024|access-date=26 December 2024}}</ref>

On 30 January 2025, Wembanyama was named as reserve for the [[2025 NBA All-Star Game]], his first selection.<ref>{{cite web| title= Victor Wembanyama, Jaylen Brown highlight 2025 All-Star Game reserves | website=NBA.com | date=30 January 2025 | url= https://www.nba.com/news/2025-nba-all-star-game-reserves | access-date=2 February 2025}}</ref> On 20 February, the Spurs shut Wembanyama down for the remainder of the season after discovering [[deep vein thrombosis]] in his right shoulder.<ref>{{cite web |title=Spurs Injury Update – 2.20.25 |url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-injury-update-2-20-25 |website=NBA.com |access-date=20 February 2025 |date=20 February 2025}}</ref> At the time the condition was discovered, he was averaging 24.3 points, 11.0 rebounds, 3.7 assists, and led the NBA with 3.8 blocks in 46 games.<ref>{{cite web|first=Jasmyn|last=Wimbish|title=Victor Wembanyama injury: Spurs star expected to miss rest of season with deep vein thrombosis in shoulder|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/victor-wembanyama-injury-spurs-star-expected-to-miss-rest-of-season-with-deep-vein-thrombosis-in-shoulder/|website=CBS Sports|date=20 February 2025|access-date=20 February 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=MacMahon |first=Tim |title=Spurs shut down Victor Wembanyama over blood clot in shoulder |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/43937353/spurs-shut-victor-wembanyama-blood-clot-shoulder |work=ESPN |date=20 February 2025 |access-date=20 February 2025}}</ref>

====2025–26 season: Unanimous Defensive Player of the Year and first NBA Finals appearance====
[[File:Victor Wembanyama San Antonio Spurs 2025 NBA Cup (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|Wembanyama with the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in 2025]]

His 40 points surpassed [[George Gervin]]'s previous record (39) for the most points scored in a season-opening game in Spurs franchise history.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/san-antonio-spurs/spurs-news-victor-wembanyama-san-antonio-record-season-opener-scoring|title=Victor Wembanyama sets Spurs record for season opener scoring|website=ClutchPoints|last=Mariano|first=Paolo|date=22 October 2025|access-date=22 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/46693030/victor-wembanyama-returns-40-point-showing-spurs-win|title=Victor Wembanyama returns with 40-point showing in Spurs' win|website=ESPN|last=Wright|first=Michael|date=22 October 2025|access-date=22 October 2025}}</ref> On 30 October, Wembanyama recorded 27 points, 18 rebounds, six assists, and five blocks to lead the [[San Antonio Spurs]] to a 107–101 victory over the [[Miami Heat]]. With the win, the Spurs improved to 5–0, marking the best start to a season in franchise history.<ref>{{cite web |title=Behind Victor Wembanyama, Spurs off to franchise-best 5-0 start |url=https://www.nba.com/news/behind-victor-wembanyama-spurs-release-years-of-frustration-with-franchise-record-start-to-season |website=NBA.com |access-date=31 October 2025 |date=31 October 2025}}</ref> On 10 November, Wembanyama put up 38 points, 12 rebounds, five assists, five blocks, and six three-pointers made in a 121–117 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]]. He became the first player to put up at least 35 points, 10 rebounds, five assists, five blocks, and five three-pointers made in a game in NBA history.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/san-antonio-spurs/spurs-news-victor-wembanyama-historic-stat-line-bulls-nba|title=Spurs' Victor Wembanyama drops historic stat line vs. Bulls not seen before in NBA|website=ClutchPoints|last=Mariano|first=Paolo|date=10 November 2025|access-date=11 November 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/breaking-news/article/victor-wembanyama-drops-38-points-cooks-nikola-vucevic-late-in-historic-outing-to-lift-spurs-past-bulls-042813543.html|title=Victor Wembanyama drops 38 points, cooks Nikola Vučević late in historic outing to lift Spurs past Bulls|last=Young|first=Ryan|website=Yahoo Sports|date=10 November 2025|access-date=11 November 2025}}</ref> On 12 November, Wembanyama recorded his 4th career triple-double with 31 points, 14 rebounds, and 10 assists in the Spurs’ 125–120 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]]. He and [[Stephon Castle]] became the first pair of teammates in Spurs history to record triple-doubles in the same game. They also became the fifth duo in NBA history to each produce a 20-point triple-double in a game.<ref>{{cite web |title=Wemby, Castle proud despite dual triple-doubles in Spurs loss |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401810075 |website=ESPN |date=13 November 2025 |access-date=13 November 2025}}</ref> On 19 December, Wembanyama put up 26 points, 12 rebounds, and two blocks in a 126–98 win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. He recorded his 100th consecutive game with at least one block made, joining [[Dikembe Mutombo]] and [[Patrick Ewing]] as the only players to record a block in at least 100 consecutive games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/san-antonio-spurs/spurs-news-victor-wembanyama-exclusive-nba-history-club-hawks|title=Spurs' Victor Wembanyama joins exclusive club in NBA history during Hawks game|website=ClutchPoints|last=Edañol|first=Yasmin|date=19 December 2025|access-date=19 December 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.philstar.com/sports/2025/12/20/2495690/wembanyama-26-point-bench-cameo-takes-spurs-hawks-win/|title=Wembanyama 26-point bench cameo takes Spurs to Hawks win|website=Philstar.com|date=20 December 2025|access-date=20 December 2025}}</ref>

On 19 January 2026, Wembanyama was named a Western Conference starter for the [[2026 NBA All-Star Game]], marking his second consecutive selection and his first as a starter.<ref>{{cite web |title=Luka Dončić, Giannis Antetokounmpo lead 2026 All-Star starters |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2026-all-star-starters |website=NBA.com |access-date=28 January 2026 |language=en}}</ref> On 10 February, Wembanyama scored 40 points and collected 12 rebounds in a 136–108 victory over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. He poured in 37 points in the first half, the highest-scoring half by a Spurs player in the 21st century, and surpassed [[Tim Duncan]] in career 40-point games, recording his sixth such performance. Wembanyama also became the third player in the past 50 seasons to score at least 40 points while playing 27 minutes or fewer.<ref>{{cite web |title=Victor Wembanyama scores 37 of 40 in 1st half, leading Spurs to 136-108 win over short-handed Lakers |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401810629
 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=11 February 2026 |date=11 February 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Open Thread: Victor Wembanyama has more 40-point games than Tim Duncan |url=https://www.poundingtherock.com/spurs-discussion-threads/94822/open-thread-victor-wembanyama-has-more-40-point-games-than-tim-duncan |website=Pounding The Rock |publisher=SB Nation |author-first1=Jeph |author-last1=Duarte |date=11 February 2026 |access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref> On 19 March, Wembanyama scored 34 points, grabbed 12 rebounds and added three steals, including a game‑winning jumper with 1.1 seconds left to lift the Spurs to a 101–100 victory over the [[Phoenix Suns]] and clinch the franchise’s first playoff berth since [[2018–19 San Antonio Spurs season|2019]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Associated Press |title=Wembanyama hits winner as Spurs beat Suns 101‑100 to end six‑season postseason drought |work=Associated Press |date=19 March 2026 |url=https://apnews.com/article/suns-spurs-score-wembanyama-booker-966084a47e84291e3b5a9c8d9d02a58d |access-date=20 March 2026}}</ref> On 1 April, Wembanyama recorded 41 points, 18 rebounds, and three blocks in a 127–113 win over the [[Golden State Warriors]]. At 22 years and 88 days, he became the youngest player to notch back-to-back 40-point, 15-rebound games and the only player in the past 50 years to record consecutive games with at least 40 points, 15 rebounds, and three blocks. He also tallied 27 points and 13 rebounds in the first half, becoming the first Spurs player with at least 25 points and 10 rebounds in any half since play-by-play tracking began in the 1997–98 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Starting 5: West win streaks continue; Thunder-Lakers looms tonight |url=https://www.nba.com/news/starting-5-april-2-2026 |access-date=2 April 2026 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}</ref> Wembanyama was named the [[NBA Defensive Player of the Year]] of the [[2025–26 NBA season]], becoming the youngest player to ever win it and the first ever player to unanimously win the award in NBA history.<ref>{{cite web |title=Spurs' Victor Wembanyama named 2025-26 Kia NBA Defensive Player of the Year |url=https://www.nba.com/news/kia-nba-defensive-player-of-the-year-award-2025-26 |website=[[NBA.com]] |publisher=Tim Reynolds |access-date=20 April 2026}}</ref> He also finished third in the [[NBA Most Valuable Player Award]] voting and earned his first [[All-NBA Team|All-NBA First Team]] selection.<ref>{{Cite web |date=17 May 2026 |title=Shai Gilgeous-Alexander becomes the 14th player to win back-to-back Kia NBA MVPs |url=https://www.nba.com/news/shai-gilgeous-alexander-kia-mvp-2025-26 |access-date=17 May 2026 |website=NBA.com|last=Reynolds|first=Tim|agency=Associated Press |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=2025–26 Kia All-NBA Teams announced |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2025-26-all-nba-teams-announced |website=NBA.com |date=24 May 2026 |access-date=27 May 2026}}</ref>

On 19 April, Wembanyama made his [[NBA playoffs]] debut in Game 1 of the [[2026 NBA playoffs#(2) San Antonio Spurs vs. (7) Portland Trail Blazers|Western Conference First Round]] against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], registering 35 points, five rebounds and five three-point field goals made in a 111–98 win, setting a franchise record for the most points scored by a Spurs player in their playoff debut, surpassing the previous record set by Tim Duncan.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Weiss |first=Jared |date=20 April 2026 |title=Victor Wembanyama’s playoff debut lives up to the Spurs’ legendary standards |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7211535/2026/04/20/victor-wembanyama-spurs-playoff-debut/ |access-date=21 April 2026 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>
In Game 2, Wembanyama suffered a concussion after tripping and hitting his head. He was ruled out for Game 3. After beating the Trail Blazers in five games, Wembanyama led the Spurs to their first playoff series win since [[2017 NBA playoffs|2017]]. He put up 27 points, 12 rebounds and seven blocks in Game 4, followed by 17 points, 14 rebounds and six blocks in Game 5. He became the first player since [[Patrick Ewing]] in [[1994 NBA playoffs|1994]] to put up consecutive double-doubles with at least six blocks in the playoffs.<ref>{{cite web |last=Zillgitt |first=Jeff |title=4 takeaways: Young San Antonio team earns its playoff spurs with series victory |url=https://www.nba.com/news/trail-blazers-spurs-2026-playoffs-first-round-game-5-takeaways |website=NBA.com |publisher=National Basketball Association |date=29 April 2026 |access-date=29 April 2026}}</ref> On 4 May, in Game 1 of the [[2026 NBA playoffs#(2) San Antonio Spurs vs. (6) Minnesota Timberwolves|Western Conference Semifinals]] against the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], Wembanyama put up a triple-double with 11 points, 15 rebounds, and 12 blocks in a 104–102 loss. His 12 blocks set the record for the most blocks in a playoff game in NBA history,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/san-antonio-spurs/victor-wembanyama-sets-nba-record-absurd-block-total-vs-timberwolves|title=Victor Wembanyama sets NBA record with absurd block total vs. Timberwolves|website=ClutchPoints|last=Reyna|first=Lorenzo|date=4 May 2026|access-date=4 May 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/playoffs/2026/05/04/victor-wembanyama-blocks-spurs-timberwolves-game-1/89940472007/|title=Victor Wembanyama sets playoff blocks record with triple-double vs. T-wolves|website=USA Today|last=Reyes|first=Lorenzo|date=4 May 2026|access-date=4 May 2026}}</ref> although [[Wilt Chamberlain]] is said to have had multiple higher totals before blocks became an officials NBA statistic in 1973, including a 16-block 1969 game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/article/victor-wembanyama-vs-wilt-chamberlain-whos-the-real-nba-block-leader-190329831.html|title=Victor Wembanyama vs. Wilt Chamberlain: Who's the real NBA block leader?|accessdate=4 June 2026|date=14 May 2026|publisher=[[Yahoo! Sports]]|author-last1=Haberstroh|author-first1= Tom}}</ref> In Game 3, Wembanyama led the Spurs to a 115–108 victory over the Minnesota Timberwolves, posting 39 points, 15 rebounds and five blocks. On 18 May, in Game 1 of the [[2026_NBA_playoffs#Western_Conference_Finals|Western Conference Finals]] against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], Wembanyama recorded 41 points and 24 rebounds, along with three assists and three blocks, leading the Spurs to a 122–115 double-overtime win.  |title=NBA Finals: Victor Wembanyama draws flagrant foul early in Game 4 loss, called for a flagrant after hitting Karl-Anthony Towns

===Junior national team===
Wembanyama represented [[France men's national under-17 basketball team|France]] at the [[2019 FIBA U16 European Championship]] in [[Udine]], Italy. In an 80–78 quarterfinal win over [[Croatia men's national under-16 and under-17 basketball team|Croatia]], he recorded 12 points, 21 rebounds and eight blocks.<ref>{{cite web |last=Rutard |first=Sacha |title=Euro U16: Propulsée par un phénoménal Victor Wembanyama (37 d'évaluation), la France se hisse en demi-finale |url=https://www.basketeurope.com/une/472148/euro-u16-propulse-par-un-phenomenal-victor-wembanyama-37-devaluation-la-france-se-hisse-en-demi-finale/ |publisher=Basket Europe |access-date=9 February 2020 |language=fr |date=14 August 2019 |archive-date=22 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230422141513/https://www.basketeurope.com/une/472148/euro-u16-propulse-par-un-phenomenal-victor-wembanyama-37-devaluation-la-france-se-hisse-en-demi-finale/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He averaged nine points, 9.6 rebounds and a tournament-leading 5.3 blocks per game, leading France to a silver medal and earning all-tournament team honours.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u16/2019/team/France|title=France at the FIBA U16 European Championship 2019|publisher=[[FIBA]]|language=en|access-date=30 October 2019|archive-date=2 November 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191102193131/https://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u16/2019/team/France|url-status=live}}</ref>

He then competed at the [[2021 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup]] in [[Latvia]]. Wembanyama averaged 14 points, 7.4 rebounds and 5.7 blocks per game, and was named to the all-tournament team after leading France to the silver medal. He recorded 22 points, eight rebounds and eight blocks in an 83–81 loss to the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chet Holmgren takes home TISSOT MVP award after helping USA to U19 World Cup title |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/world/u19/2021/news/chet-holmgren-takes-home-tissot-mvp-award-after-helping-usa-to-u19-world-cup-title |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=12 July 2021 |date=11 July 2021 |archive-date=19 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220519203736/https://www.fiba.basketball/world/u19/2021/news/chet-holmgren-takes-home-tissot-mvp-award-after-helping-usa-to-u19-world-cup-title |url-status=live }}</ref> Wembanyama set the FIBA record for blocks per game in a single tournament.<ref>{{cite web |last=Rutard |first=Sacha |title=Victor Wembanyama a battu, à la Coupe du Monde U19, le record de contres pour un évènement FIBA ! |url=https://www.basketeurope.com/livenews-fr/558149/victor-wembanyama-a-battu-a-la-coupe-du-monde-u19-le-record-de-contres-pour-un-evenement-fiba/ |publisher=Basket Europe |language=fr |access-date=23 August 2021 |date=17 July 2021 |archive-date=23 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230423093245/https://www.basketeurope.com/livenews-fr/558149/victor-wembanyama-a-battu-a-la-coupe-du-monde-u19-le-record-de-contres-pour-un-evenement-fiba/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

==== 2024 Summer Olympics ====
[[File:Victor Wembanyama, July 2024.jpg|thumb|Wembanyama with [[France men's national basketball team|France]] in 2024]]
Wembanyama was selected for France to play at the [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2024 Summer Olympics]], which were held in his native Paris.<ref>{{Cite news |date=21 March 2024 |title=Victor Wembanyama, sur les JO de Paris : " La médaille d'or est très atteignable " |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Jo-2024-paris/Basket/Actualites/Victor-wembanyama-sur-les-jo-de-paris-la-medaille-d-or-est-tres-atteignable/1456044}}</ref> He had 19 points and 9 rebounds in his Olympic debut in a win against [[Brazil men's national basketball team|Brazil]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 July 2024 |title=Wemby showed Alien-like nature in Olympic debut |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/mens-olympic-basketball-tournament-paris-2024/news/wemby-showed-alien-like-nature-in-olympic-debut |access-date=11 August 2024 |website=www.fiba.basketball |language=en}}</ref> Wembanyama helped France reach its second consecutive final, following a quarterfinal win over [[Canada men's national basketball team|Canada]] and semifinal win over [[Germany men's national basketball team|Germany]], in which they faced the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States]]. == Personal life ==
[[File:Victor Wembanyama NBA Paris Game.jpg|thumb|upright|alt=Wembanyama watching a NBA game from off the court.|Wembanyama sitting courtside at an [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] game in Paris in 2023]]

Wembanyama is represented by [[sports agent|agent]] Bouna Ndiaye of Comsport. His family has a longtime relationship with Ndiaye, whose son was coached by Wembanyama's mother from an early age. Ndiaye has advised Wembanyama since he was 15 years old, then signed him as a client in 2022.<ref name="mullen">{{cite web |last=Mullen |first=Liz |title=Labor and Agents: French Connection: How agent for projected top NBA Draft pick built his practice |url=https://www.sportsbusinessjournal.com/Journal/Issues/2023/01/09/Insiders/labor-and-agents.aspx |website=Sports Business Journal |access-date=16 January 2023 |date=9 January 2023 |archive-date=14 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230314183053/https://www.sportsbusinessjournal.com/Journal/Issues/2023/01/09/Insiders/labor-and-agents.aspx |url-status=live }}</ref>

Wembanyama was a year ahead for his age in school and attended [[Secondary education in France#Lycée|lycée]] in agreement with Nanterre 92.
